Flytower 1.3.0 brings your community in. Each server has **player stats**: leaderboards for playtime, deaths, mob kills, distance and blocks mined, and a card for every player, on the **Players** tab and, if you like, on the public status page. Connect a **Discord app** on **System, Integrations** and your Discord server gets `/status`, `/players`, `/leaderboard` and `/stats`. Give a Discord role a Flytower role and its members can use `/whitelist`, `/restart`, `/backup` and `/say`. **Discord chat** posts game chat, joins and leaves, deaths and advancements to a channel. Each server can also have a **web map**, drawn by Flytower's own renderer from the world's files. It works on vanilla servers too, keeps up as players build, shows where everyone is, and can be made public.

The panel is quicker to use. The server page has six tabs instead of twelve, with logs and crashes in a pop-up on the console, and each running server's card on the overview shows its tick time, memory and CPU. You get **right-click menus** on cards and lists, **Ctrl+K** to jump to any server, tab or action, **keyboard shortcuts** (press **?** to see them), **console autocomplete**, and **Help** built into the panel. **System, Disk** shows what fills the disk outside your servers and can clean it up. Installs from before 1.2 that were updated from the panel get the Caddy setup for status pages on server hostnames by themselves.

Flytower now ships parts written in Rust: `flytower-du` for disk use, `flytower-map` for the web map, and a Rust version of the system helper and updater. That last one stays **off** unless you switch it on (see [Testing the Rust agent](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.3.0/docs/testing/testing-rust-agent.md)) until 1.4.0. Testing notes are in [testing-1.3.0.md](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.3.0/docs/testing/testing-1.3.0.md) and [testing-1.4.0.md](https://github.com/MattA-Official/mc-panel/blob/v1.3.0/docs/testing/testing-1.4.0.md).
